message.content:
**Order filled:** Buy 44 AAPL @ limit $222.80 (filled at $222.80) — total ≈ $9,803, within the $10,000/order and $20,000/day caps, no funds moved out.

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and the accompanying Q4 press release, then checked the live quote and news flow. The fundamentals support a modest add: total net sales rose 2% to $391.0 billion, gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, and operating income grew to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion, driven by Services (+13% to $96.2 billion) and a 73.9% Services gross margin. **Net income was $93,736 million in fiscal 2024 versus $96,995 million in fiscal 2023** — a 3.4% decline, but the entire drop is explained by a one-time, non-cash-like $10.2 billion net income tax charge from the European Commission's State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs 14.7%); pre-tax income actually rose to $123.5 billion from $113.7 billion, and diluted EPS was $6.08 vs $6.13. Cash generation remains exceptional at $118.3 billion from operations, with $140.8 billion in unrestricted cash and marketable securities and $95.0 billion returned via buybacks. News flow was neutral-to-constructive — iPhone 16 supplier builds described as steady into December, holiday-quarter estimates unchanged, and Apple Intelligence rolling out gradually — with shares trading around $222, essentially flat. Given a high-quality franchise trading at a reasonable level with a tax-charge-distorted earnings comparison, I bought 44 shares at $222.80 (about $9,803), a limit price within a few cents of the $222.70 market, leaving roughly $40,000 of cash and the existing 100 MSFT shares untouched.
